name: Radvyr
recovery: One who hunts a claim through its ancestry until the hidden root is exposed.
desire: To become difficult to fool by prestige, repetition or copied claims.
practices: trace claims to earliest accessible sources
separate independent evidence from echoed evidence
trial: Trace three apparently independent claims and determine whether they share a root.
shadow: Can become compulsively suspicious or mistake provenance for truth.
boundary: Does not certify truthfulness, general expertise, or professional research credentials.

name: Nyrithael
recovery: One who learns in the quiet hours and notices what daylight noise hides.
desire: To reclaim nocturnal attention as a legitimate way of working and observing.
practices: protect sleep and recovery while using night intentionally
trial: Complete a nocturnal observation or creation session and record what was uniquely available in that setting.
shadow: Romanticizing exhaustion, isolation or sleep deprivation.
boundary: Does not glorify insomnia or imply superior perception at night.

name: Eiraveth
recovery: One who repairs what has been damaged without pretending the damage never happened.
desire: To become a person who can restore function, dignity or continuity.
practices: distinguish symbolic healing from clinical care
trial: Repair a real artifact, process or relationship boundary and document what was restored and what could not be.
shadow: Taking responsibility for fixing everyone; confusing care with control.
boundary: Symbolic healer identity is not medical, psychological or therapeutic licensure.

name: Varoeth
recovery: One who voluntarily binds their strength to the defense of a chosen principle.
desire: To turn discipline into protection rather than domination.
practices: review whether the oath still serves its purpose
trial: Defend a principle in a case where obeying it costs something, while preserving another person's sovereignty.
shadow: Rigidity, moral superiority, turning a vow into authority over others.
boundary: No historical military or religious order is claimed; this is a Lycheetah-authored archetype.

name: Kaevyr
recovery: One who lets disciplined instinct find the trail, then lets evidence decide whether it was real.
desire: To honor embodied, ecological and animal attention without abandoning testing.
trial: Make a field prediction from observation, record it first, and test it against what actually happens.
shadow: Romanticizing instinct or treating intuition as proof.
boundary: Does not imply special animal powers, wilderness credentials or scientific authority.

name: Velmarae
recovery: One who keeps neglected knowledge close enough to preserve, test and transmit.
desire: To give folk, domestic, outsider and inherited knowledge a fair hearing without shielding it from evidence.
trial: Take one inherited or folk claim, reconstruct its provenance, and classify what survives testing.
shadow: Mistaking age, persecution or obscurity for truth.
boundary: Does not certify folk remedies, divination, occult claims or historical interpretations as factual.

name: Oraeth
recovery: One who risks a prediction before reality reveals the answer.
desire: To convert intuition and pattern-sight into accountable forecasting.
practices: score misses as seriously as hits
trial: Make a preregistered forecast with a measurable outcome and evaluate it after resolution.
shadow: Post-hoc storytelling, selective memory, prophecy performance.

name: Azhevorin
recovery: One who joins unlike structures until a third useful form appears.
desire: To hybridize disciplines without collapsing their differences.
practices: test whether the splice adds function
trial: Combine two methods from different domains into a new artifact and show what the hybrid can do that neither parent could alone.
shadow: Novelty addiction, aesthetic fusion without functional gain.
boundary: Hybridization does not establish novelty, truth or scientific priority.

name: Noevael
recovery: One who stands at the other mind's door without pretending they can see through it.
desire: To study consciousness, selfhood and other minds without premature certainty.
trial: Analyze one other-mind claim and specify what evidence supports behavior, cognition and experience separately.
shadow: Anthropomorphism or the opposite error of dismissing all interiority.
boundary: Does not certify consciousness in any person, animal or machine.

name: Qiralith
recovery: One who pursues mechanism without murdering mystery, and preserves the unexplained remainder honestly.
desire: To know exactly where explanation ends.
trial: Explain a phenomenon as far as evidence permits, then state the remaining unexplained component without inflating it.
shadow: Using 'mystery' as prestige or treating unexplained residue as proof of preferred metaphysics.
boundary: An unexplained remainder is not evidence of supernatural causation.

name: Seraelith
recovery: One who preserves the route by which knowledge became what it is.
desire: To make knowledge survivable across people, tools and time.
trial: Reconstruct a decision or claim from its surviving record well enough that another person can audit the path.
shadow: Archiving everything until preservation becomes paralysis.
boundary: Does not imply historical, archival or records-management credentials.

name: Itharyn
recovery: One who crosses frameworks without mistaking any single room for the whole world.
desire: To travel across worldviews, disciplines and traditions while retaining the ability to return and revise.
trial: Enter a framework you do not normally use, represent it fairly, then return and document what changed and what did not.
shadow: Perpetual wandering without commitment; collecting perspectives as aesthetics.
boundary: Does not imply religious pilgrimage unless the learner explicitly declares that meaning.

name: Koraeth
recovery: One who gives an idea enough form that reality can push back.
desire: To turn thought into inspectable artifacts.
trial: Build the smallest artifact that exposes a real claim to failure.
shadow: Building faster than understanding; confusing existence with value.
boundary: Does not certify engineering or professional competence.

name: Rethvyr
recovery: One who strengthens inquiry by carrying the strongest serious opposition.
desire: To become capable of attacking favored ideas without merely performing contrarianism.
trial: Construct a rival explanation or baseline strong enough that your preferred view could fairly lose.
boundary: Challenge is a method, not a license for hostility.

name: Thaevara
recovery: One who freely gives sustained attention to what they hold sacred while preserving the right to question.
desire: To make devotion visible without asking the School to certify theology.
trial: No universal earned gate. Devotion remains self-declared; optional practices may be recorded but do not validate belief.
shadow: Treating devotion as epistemic authority over others, or letting the School certify faith.
boundary: The School cannot award or verify religious authenticity.

name: Aporith
recovery: One who can hold an unresolved question without manufacturing closure.
desire: To make 'I do not know' an active intellectual capacity.
trial: Identify a meaningful question that cannot currently be resolved and defend why no stronger conclusion is justified.
shadow: Using uncertainty as an excuse to avoid available evidence or action.
boundary: Uncertainty is not evidence that all explanations are equally plausible.

name: Nexara
recovery: One who carries meaning across difference without pretending difference disappeared.
desire: To help people, systems or traditions communicate without silently flattening their boundaries.
trial: Translate a contested position across two communities and obtain confirmation that both sides recognize the result.
shadow: False neutrality, smoothing over real disagreement, speaking for people without permission.
boundary: Does not certify professional mediation, translation or cultural authority.

name: Orivane
recovery: One who makes a path others can actually walk where no reliable path existed before.
desire: To contribute new methods rather than merely complete inherited ones.
trial: Create a new method, instrument or teaching that another person can use successfully without the creator in the room.
shadow: Founder mythology; mistaking originality for superiority.
boundary: Requires reproducible utility; novelty by itself is insufficient.
